- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bracing yourself is an essential technique for maintaining a neutral spine and preventing back pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] You should brace yourself whenever you're doing anything that puts stress on your spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Activities that may require you to brace yourself include lifting heavy objects, bending over, sitting for long periods, standing for long periods, and during exercise.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When lifting heavy objects, you should maintain a neutral spine and engage your core muscles before lifting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When bending over, you should engage your core muscles and maintain a neutral spine to protect your back.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To protect your back while sitting for long periods, you should brace yourself by engaging your core muscles and maintaining a neutral spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To prevent back pain while standing for long periods, you should brace yourself by engaging your core muscles and maintaining a neutral spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During exercise, you should brace yourself by engaging your core muscles and maintaining a neutral spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bracing yourself is a technique that should be used in any situation where you need to protect your spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Exercises that target your core muscles can help you develop the strength and stability needed to brace yourself.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Exercises for bracing yourself include: 
  1. Planks: Hold for 30 seconds to 1 minute, repeat for 3 to 5 sets.
  2. Dead Bugs: Aim for 3 sets of 10 repetitions on each side.
  3. Bird Dogs: Aim for 3 sets of 10 repetitions on each side.
  4. Side Planks: Hold for 30 seconds to 1 minute, aim for 3 sets on each side.
  5. Hollow Body Hold: Hold for 30 seconds to 1 minute, repeat for 3 to 5 sets.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Start slowly and gradually increase the intensity of these exercises as you get stronger.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Always listen to your body, and stop immediately if you feel any pain or discomfort.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for maintaining good posture throughout the day include using ergonomic furniture, sitting and standing correctly, taking breaks, using a lumbar roll, strengthening your core, and being mindful of your posture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When sitting, your feet should be flat on the floor, and your hips should be positioned at a 90-degree angle.
